Subject: Post-demo: hyperscaler comparison + air-gapped POC plan

Hi Elena — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we all have a single view: 

What we demo'd
- Live inference on a 4k context (Redwood Dedicated runtime) with prefix caching and continuous batching turned on. Demo emphasized predictable p50/p95 latency under steady load.
- Control plane options: hosted control plane (default), customer-managed control plane (VPC peering), and air-gapped private bundle for on-prem installs.

How we differentiate from hyperscaler offerings (short list)
- Predictable unit economics: token-level breakdown + cost controls so you can cap per-route spend.
- Smart routing and graceful fallback: policy-based routing to lower-cost variants and automatic regional fallbacks.
- Production-first tooling: tracing, per-route SLOs, and canary rollouts for model version changes.
- Private deployments: support for customer-managed control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, and an air-gap path that preserves audit logs + offline rollout.

Specific asks / next tests we agreed
1) FinServ will provide a short workload snapshot (sample requests + typical concurrency) so we can size the Dedicated pool and generate expected cost estimates. (Elena: you said ~300 QPS peak, confirm.)
2) Networking test: we'll run a control-plane proxy connectivity test (TCP/443) from your staging VLAN to our control plane proxy. Karthik will own the test config.
3) Air-gap smoke test: provide IP ranges and a short window for us to deliver an air-gap bundle and smoke test checklist (we'll need certs + a staging HSM/KMS endpoint).
4) Procurement: procurement contact + any required NDA/PO templates.

Attachments: redwood-hyperscaler-differentiators.pdf (one-page summary), controlplane-networking-checklist.xlsx, poa-airgap-smoke-test-plan.docx

Proposed timeline
- By EOD Thu (2026-12-23): we’ll send a tailored cost estimate and a technical runbook for the networking test.
- Week of Jan 4: control plane proxy test and air-gap smoke window (if your team is available).

Ben and Karthik are looped for technical clarifications — we’ll defer to them on specifics if anything needs deeper detail.

Thanks — Stephanie

Thanks Stephanie — great session. A couple of clarifying questions before we share the workload snapshot: 

1) Air-gapped feasibility: when you say "air-gap bundle" what exactly does that include? Will we have to open any outbound connections during normal operation? Our security team is highly restrictive.
2) Control plane: if we choose the customer-managed control plane (VPC peering), do you still require a persistent control-plane connection back to Redwood for telemetry/rollouts? We need to understand data flows and whether keys/certs ever leave our network.
3) HSM/KMS: can you support our on-prem HSM (Thales Luna) for signing models, or do we need to route through a cloud KMS?
4) Pricing ballpark: we need a rough monthly cost range for a Dedicated pool sized for ~300 QPS and for a private air-gapped deployment (one-time infra + monthly maintenance).

Procurement contact: procurement@finserv.com — they asked for an NDA before any PoC technical artifacts are exchanged.

If you can answer the bullets above, I’ll share the workload snapshot and we can schedule the networking test.

—Elena

Elena — adding details to the great summary Stephanie sent and answering your questions inline: 

1) Air-gap bundle contents and connectivity
- The air-gap bundle is an installer + runtime tarball that contains the inference runtime, a minimal control plane shim that can operate offline, and a local admin UI.
- During normal operation the air-gapped runtime does NOT require outbound connectivity. For upgrades/telemetry you can opt into an out-of-band sync window initiated from your side (we provide a signed package to import).

2) Customer-managed control plane (VPC peering)
- With VPC peering the control messages (rollouts, routing decisions) flow over the peered connection. We do not persist any customer data in our hosted control plane for that mode; logs can be forwarded to your logging endpoint.
- If you elect a fully hosted control plane we surface telemetry metadata (latency/cost) but payloads stay in your region. Persistent egress is required for hosted mode only.

3) HSM/KMS support
- We support BYO-HSM for signing keys; integration with Thales Luna is on our supported integrations list. We'll need you to provide an API-enablement window to validate signing operations during the smoke test.

4) Pricing ballpark (very rough)
- Dedicated pool (300 QPS baseline): $28k–$45k/mo depending on instance class, slot config, and desired p50/p95 targets.
- Air-gapped on-prem: one-time packaging & onsite assistance $45k–$90k, monthly maintenance/patch service $4k–$10k/mo.

Next tests I propose
- Networking probe: Karthik will send a small test harness you can run from your staging VLAN (simple curl-based connectivity to our control-plane proxy on port 443).
- HSM sign test: we exchange test cert and run a signing handshake inside your staging environment (no keys leave your network).
- Throughput smoke: minimal on-prem deployment (single rack) to run your 4k-context workload for 1 hour and collect p50/p95 and token cost metrics.

Karthik will follow up with the exact commands and a proposed window — tagging him here.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
